title: Data and normalization interfaces for adic ring/module systems
statement: Let $(C,J)$ be an essentially small site relative to a coefficient universe and let $I$ be an index category. A diagram of ring/module pairs consists of a diagram $R_i$ of commutative-ring sheaves, a diagram $P_i$ of additive sheaves, an $R_i$-module sheaf $M_i$, and additive identifications $U(M_i)\cong P_i$, with semilinear transition maps [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Its underlying ring and module diagrams and its presented action are obtained by forgetting operations and conjugating through these identifications. A comparison over a left exact set-sheaf inverse image consists of algebraic inverse-image lifts and module isomorphisms whose ring and module squares commute [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. For a positive-index coefficient tower, record the full ring limit, a strided subsequence identified with the level ring diagram, the additive limit of the module tower, projection compatibility with scalar action, and naturality in $I$ [def-pur-sheaf-inverse-limit]. Local bases mean one cover per $i$ with compatible rank-one bases on the localized sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. A localization is a pair diagram identified with the actual fraction-ring sheaves and scalar localizations, with normalized natural units [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. A filtered colimit is a ring and additive colimit carrying a module action whose formula on two stage sections is the common-upper-bound formula [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Cofinal restriction, integral normalization, localization normalization and colimit comparison name the corresponding projection, unit and coprojection equations. All these records contain actual data and properties, and none asserts the existence of a base-change comparison.
